long_biography.plain_text:
Goemans entered the family enterprise created by his father, Peter, who had opened a Cannes perfume shop before bringing European luxury goods to Japan. Michel took the helm with Catherine in 1967. Together they developed premium-fashion boutiques and operating networks across Hong Kong, Singapore and Guam, establishing Bluebell as a bridge between European houses and Asian consumers.

Bluebell's partnerships expanded from perfume and fashion into a broad luxury and lifestyle portfolio, including an early Asian relationship with Louis Vuitton. Goemans combined inherited access with long-term commercial leadership rather than passive family shareholding. Later generations moved into executive roles, while current corporate materials describe a multi-market group serving more than 150 brand partners. His principal business identity remains the development of luxury distribution and retail across Asia.

The book shortens the vessel name, and the authoritative August 1974 relationship start predates the broker's 1978 delivery year, so the bridge is very strong but not treated as a registry-derived title chain or exact build-date reconciliation.
